q: The topological entropy of a substitution tiling (like Penrose tiling) is:
opts: Zero, since substitution tilings are repetitive (every patch recurs) and complexity p(n) grows polynomially
exp: Substitution tilings (Penrose, Ammann-Beenker, etc.) have polynomial patch complexity (number of distinct patches of size n grows polynomially in n), giving zero topological entropy. Despite having uncountably many distinct tilings, they are 'ordered' (zero entropy, not chaotic).
